Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown

many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

out=[[9]*15 for _ in range(28)]

 for c in range(5,10):out[r][c]=4
# algorithm file specific: detect bbox largest non-bg-color object and fill rectangle, clear extras
code='''def transform(grid):\n    bg=9\n    pts=[(r,c) for r,row in enumerate(grid) for c,v in enumerate(row) if v==4]\n    r0=min(r for r,c in pts); r1=max(r for r,c in pts); c0=min(c for r,c in pts); c1=max(c for r,c in pts)\n    out=[[bg for _ in row] for row in grid]\n    for r in range(r0,r1+1):\n        for c in range(c0,c1+1): out[r][c]=4\n    return out\n'''
